title: Who's Who: Emil Hartmann
summary: Cipher designer whose work remains part of the record of modern Eidetics.
author: Who's Who Desk
paragraphs: The Correspondent adds Emil Hartmann (born 1832) to its Who's Who of Eideticians, recording a cipher designer whose name still attends serious discussion of the Eidetic Stratum.

Hartmann devised compact codes for sonance relays after merchants discovered that an overheard fragment could resemble an entirely different message. His celebrated sealed-almanac test caught a relay clerk adding plausible words to a damaged transmission.
He argues that a message must preserve its uncertainty along with its content.

For Alderwick readers, Emil Hartmann stands not as an ornament to legend but as a figure whose work helps explain why Eideticians prize careful terms, repeatable evidence and a sober account of what remains unknown.
